findings.evidence: Both lemmas in each pair key on the same head term, e.g. `quarkKinetic_apply` LHS `quarkKinetic β γ ψ Dψ μ ν = ...` (:106) vs `quarkKinetic_apply_of_isHermitian` LHS `quarkKinetic β γ ψ Dψ μ ν = (star ψ ⬝ᵥ (β * γ μ) *ᵥ (I • Dψ ν)).re` (:159), whose hypothesis `(β * γ μ).IsHermitian` simp cannot discharge. The merged precedent (`maxwellTensor_def`, `gluonPart_def`) does not cover this: those files have no competing lemma on the same LHS.
findings.fix: Drop `@[simp]` from `quarkKinetic_apply`, `quarkPart_def`, `diracOpApply_def` and `total_def`, keeping them as plain `(rfl)` restatements for explicit `rw`. Annotate the normal forms instead: `@[simp]` on `isSymm_quarkPart` and `isSymm_total` (both close their goal, and `isSymm_quarkPart` is hypothesis-free).
findings.issue: `@[simp] quarkKinetic_apply` has LHS `quarkKinetic β γ ψ Dψ μ ν`, identical to the LHS of `quarkKinetic_apply_of_isHermitian` (:157) and `ofReal_quarkKinetic_apply` (:144). The unconditional lemma carries no side goal, so simp always fires it first and the "Hermitian working form" the module docstring advertises (:58) is unreachable by simp. Same collision at the three other unfolding lemmas: `@[simp] quarkPart_def` (:116) rewrites `quarkPart` away before `isSymm_quarkPart` (:123), `quarkPart_apply_of_isHermitian` (:182), `quarkPart_mulVec` (:204), `quarkPart_equivariant` (:254) or `trace_quarkPart` (:283) can match; `@[simp] diracOpApply_def` (:269) destroys the shape of the hypothesis `diracOpApply g γ Dψ = M *ᵥ ψ` that `trace_quarkPart_of_diracEq` (:293) and `trace_total_of_diracEq` (Total.lean:126) require; `@[simp] total_def` (Total.lean:84) does the same for `isSymm_total`, `total_mulVec_gaugeRotate`, `total_equivariant` and `trace_total`.

findings.evidence: `rw [quarkPart_def, Matrix.smul_apply, Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.transpose_apply, smul_eq_mul, ...]` appears identically at QuarkPart.lean:173-174 and :187-188.
findings.fix: Add `quarkPart_apply : quarkPart β γ ψ Dψ μ ν = (quarkKinetic β γ ψ Dψ μ ν + quarkKinetic β γ ψ Dψ ν μ) / 2` and use it to open `ofReal_quarkPart_apply` and `quarkPart_apply_of_isHermitian`.
findings.issue: `quarkPart` has no entry-level `_apply` lemma. Every consumer wanting an entry must redo the `smul_apply`/`add_apply`/`transpose_apply`/`smul_eq_mul` plumbing by hand, as both proofs in this file do verbatim (lines 173-174 and 187-188). `quarkKinetic` and `gaugeRotate` both get such a lemma; `quarkPart` does not.

summary: The surface is minimal and the characteristic API is broadly complete, but the `@[simp]` unfolding lemmas collide with the files' own characteristic lemmas: the unconditional `quarkKinetic_apply`/`quarkPart_def`/`diracOpApply_def`/`total_def` always win over the Hermitian working forms, the invariance/trace lemmas, and the Dirac-equation hypothesis shape. `quarkPart` also lacks the entry-level `_apply` lemma its own proofs open-code twice.
